correctness.rationale: The published Sylvester patterns give centered representatives \( (2t,2t,2t,-3t,-3t) \) and \( (s,s,s,s,-4s) \). Direct elementary-symmetric expansion yields the stated parametrizations. Exact elimination gives the two prime ideals; each reduces to a nondegenerate plane cusp equation, and the sum ideal has quotient basis \(1,u_2,u_3\), hence length \(3\). The bundled checker reconstructs these steps from scratch over the rationals.

value.rationale: The source leaves the meeting of the two singular-locus curves at the maximally symmetric Clebsch cubic only set-theoretic. Determining that both branches are themselves cuspidal and have contact length three supplies the first local scheme structure at this distinguished intersection, clarifying how the two surface components' common curves degenerate at the point with maximal \(S_5\) symmetry. The invariant-coordinate calculation is exact, natural, and reusable in further local study of the Eckardt divisor.
